newsitem.title: JAPAN: JR West shares seen having ample room to grow.
newsitem.headline: JR West shares seen having ample room to grow.

text.p: The much-awaited results of bidding for shares in West Japan Railways Corp (JR West) on Tuesday indicated that the stock price may be modest, avoiding roller-coaster levels of previous privatisation issues.
"Judging from the auction results, the initial offer price will probably be set at around 350,000 yen ($3,240)," Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities said.
"A modest share price will mean more gains for investors, unlike in the past where the initial prices started high and then declined," he said.
Shares in JR West, part of the formerly state-owned Japan Railways group, will be listed on bourses on October 8.
JR West, operator of passenger train services in the western part of Japan's main island of Honshu, is planning to sell 1.7 million shares of the two million that have been already issued.
The state-owned Japan Railways (JNR) Settlement Corp which currently owns all of the shares of JR West said it accepted 675,100 bids for the 750,000 shares offered in the auction.

JNR said the highest bid for the JR West shares in the auction was 500,000 yen ($4,629) and the lowest was 282,000 yen ($2,611,) with the largest number of bids concentrated in the 350,000 yen ($3,240) to 360,000 yen ($3,333) range.
The fixed price, based on the auction results for the shares offered outside the auction, will be announced on August 29.
In the past, privatised firms' fixed share prices were set at high levels, based on belief that newly issued shares get off to a strong start.
But expectant investors in Japan Tobacco Corp got a nasty shock when the myth crumbled.

The shares were initially sold at a hefty 1,438,000 yen ($13,300) per share when the monopoly went public in October 1994, but quotations have never surpassed the public offer price. It ended trading on Tuesday at 802,000 yen ($7,425).

"Investors who bought Japan Tobacco shares on expectations that the shares would rise were sadly disappointed and there was a rush to sell the shares before they fell too far," an analyst at a second-tier brokerage said.

The current, subdued atmosphere of the Tokyo stock market due to uncertainties over the state of the economy as well as lingering fears of an interest rate hike, is a favourable atmosphere for the JR West debut, market sources said.
"Investors are in a cautious mood, so there should not be a buying frenzy, which could send prices soaring in the initial days of trading, like the JR East shares," Nikko's Ueki said.
The public offer price of the first railway to list, East Japan Railways Corp, was 380,000 yen ($3,518).
Active trade sent the shares surging soon after it listed in October 1993. It peaked at 614,000 on October 27 and then plunged to a lifetime low of 389,000 in November.
The railway's shares ended at 519,000 yen ($4,805) on Tuesday on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
